title: matrix4x4 operator[] is broken

labels.name: Bug
labels.description: Global flag to mark a deviation from expected behaviour

body:
The operator[] of matrix4x4 gives me nonsense values, probably from uninitialized memory. According to the comment in [matrix4x4.inl:243](https://github.com/assimp/assimp/blob/c318d648ff73aa2e32b783709d69740ac3e8c072/include/assimp/matrix4x4.inl#L243), that's a known problem.

Code snippet that reproduces the problem:

```
aiMatrix4x4 transform = node->mTransformation;

std::cout <<  "  BROKEN: " << std::endl
          << std::fixed
          << "[ " << *transform[0]  << " \t" << *transform[1]  << " \t" << *transform[2]  << " \t" << *transform[3]  << std::endl
          << "  " << *transform[4]  << " \t" << *transform[5]  << " \t" << *transform[6]  << " \t" << *transform[7]  << std::endl
          << "  " << *transform[8]  << " \t" << *transform[9]  << " \t" << *transform[10] << " \t" << *transform[11] << std::endl
          << "  " << *transform[12] << " \t" << *transform[13] << " \t" << *transform[14] << " \t" << *transform[15] << " ]" << std::endl<std::endl;

std::cout << "  WORKING:" << std::endl
          << std::fixed
          << "[ " << transform.a1 << " \t" << transform.a2 << " \t" << transform.a3 << " \t" << transform.a4 << std::endl
          << "  " << transform.b1 << " \t" << transform.b2 << " \t" << transform.b3 << " \t" << transform.b4 << std::endl
          << "  " << transform.c1 << " \t" << transform.c2 << " \t" << transform.c3 << " \t" << transform.c4 << std::endl
          << "  " << transform.d1 << " \t" << transform.d2 << " \t" << transform.d3 << " \t" << transform.d4 << " ]" << std::endl;
```

Output:

```
  BROKEN:
[ 1.000000  0.000000    0.000000    0.000000
  -6383549033750467933401407029248.000000   -6383573212266860225984901152768.000000     -322887.250000  -322887.281250
  -322889.093750    -6444387016696754531989320630272.000000     -322887.250000  0.000000
  0.000000  0.000000    0.000000    0.000000 ]

  WORKING:
[ 1.000000  0.000000    0.000000    0.000000
  0.000000  1.000000    0.000000    0.000000
  0.000000  0.000000    1.000000    0.000000
  0.000000  0.000000    0.000000    1.000000 ]
```
